subject: Evaluation timeline, MAP commitments, and SLO concessions
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Smith <j.smith@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 1 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Evaluation timeline, MAP commitments, and SLO concessions

Jordan —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Per our conversation I put together a concise mutual action plan (attached) that ties the evaluation milestones to the commercial terms we're discussing. Key points:

- POC: 4-week evaluation, production-like dataset (subset) and a single-region dedicated test pool (target start: 7/6).
- Milestones: Week 1: baseline bench (latency + throughput), Week 2: optimization pass (batching/quant), Week 3: scale test, Week 4: final acceptance.
- Performance SLO ask: p95 inference latency <= 200ms for the primary workload profile during the acceptance window.
- Commercial linkage: if Acme signs a 12-month reserved commit within 30 days of acceptance, Redwood will offer an up-front credit and ramped discount schedule tied to committed spend and achieved SLOs.
  - Example: 18% discount at $120k/mo committed start, increasing to 25% when monthly committed throughput >= 70% of baseline by month 3.
  - SLA concessions: service credits for missed SLOs (detailed in attached SLA appendix).

To keep the evaluation tight we need confirmation by EOD 7/2 on: dataset access, a single technical contact for the test, and whether procurement prefers an initial 30/60/90 payment cadence.

I've attached: Redwood_MAP_v1.xlsx and a draft SLA appendix that outlines measurement windows and credit calculations.

If that looks ok I'd like to schedule a 30-minute readout at the end of Week 2 to validate optimizations and lock the commercial cadence.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Enterprise Sales Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood_MAP_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet), SLA-Draft-Appendix.pdf (pdf)
From: Jordan Smith <j.smith@acmehealth.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@acmehealth.com>
Date: Fri, 2 Jul 2026 11:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Evaluation timeline, MAP commitments, and SLO concessions

Aditya —

Thanks for the clear plan and for pulling together the MAP. A few quick clarifications from our side before we lock dates:

1) SLO target: 200ms p95 is aggressive for our clinical workload. Can we discuss a stepped SLO (e.g., p95 <= 350ms for POC acceptance, with an objective to hit 200ms by month 3 of production)?
2) Credits: procurement will need a clear table showing credits by severity/recurrence; can you confirm the maximum monthly credit percentage?
3) Commit timing: legal prefers a 60-day review after acceptance before full financial commit. Would Redwood be willing to offer interim credits or reduced pricing during that review window?

We can provide dataset access by 7/5 and assign our ML infra lead (cc'd later) as the technical contact.

Best,
Jordan Smith
Director of ML Platforms
Acme Health

Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 2 Jul 2026 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Evaluation timeline, MAP commitments, and SLO concessions (internal)

Team —

Quick internal posture so we respond with a consistent position. Summary of what I'd propose:

- Acceptance SLO: agree to a stepped approach as Jordan suggests: POC acceptance p95 <= 350ms, production objective p95 <= 200ms by month 3. This keeps POC achievable while protecting our long-term performance commitment.
- Commercial trade: offer a 20% introductory discount at signing for a 12‑month commit at $100k+/mo, escalator to 28% when ramp thresholds are met (70% utilization by month 3).
- SLA credits: cap monthly service credits at 7.5% of that month's invoice; additional remediation support option (free optimization pass) for repeat misses.
- Interim pricing during legal review (60d): provide a temporary 10% credit/holdback that converts to invoice credit if we fail to reach production SLO within the first 90 days post-acceptance. This directly addresses procurement's ask for protection during review.

Action items: Aditya to present this counter to Acme today; Tessa to cue Legal on preparing a short amendment and a one-page SLA appendix; Monica to model the economics for the different ramp scenarios and provide a recommended floor by EOD 7/3.

-Lauren
VP, Commercial

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Smith <j.smith@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 5 Jul 2026 08:46:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Evaluation timeline, MAP commitments, and SLO concessions

Jordan —

Appreciate the quick turnaround and the pragmatic ask. Per our internal alignment (summary below) Redwood can accept the stepped SLO approach and the 60-day legal review cadence with these commercial concessions:

- POC acceptance: p95 <= 350ms (during Week 4 acceptance window).
- Production objective: p95 <= 200ms by the end of month 3 post-production cutover.
- Pricing/discounts: 20% starting discount for a 12-month reserve at $100k+/mo committed spend, escalating to 28% when monthly committed throughput >= 70% of baseline by month 3.
- SLA credits: capped at 7.5% of monthly invoice (applies only after production cutover).
- Legal review protection: a 10% interim credit during the 60-day review that converts to invoice credit if production SLOs are missed in first 90 days after cutover.

I've attached an updated MAP (Redwood_MAP_v1.xlsx) and the SLA appendix for your procurement team to review. If that is acceptable I'd like to propose:

- Technical kickoff: 7/6 (dataset handoff)
- POC end & readout: week of 8/3
- Commercial signature target: within 30 days of acceptance (we can be flexible to move to 60 days with the interim credit).

Can you confirm dataset access and whether procurement needs us to route the SLA appendix via their standard DocuSign template? I'll set up a 30-minute checkpoint for 7/17 to review Week 2 progress and tweak the MAP if necessary.

Thanks,
Aditya

Attachments: Redwood_MAP_v1.xlsx, SLA-Draft-Appendix.pdf
From: Jordan Smith <j.smith@acmehealth.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Evaluation timeline, MAP commitments, and SLO concessions

Aditya —

This looks good and addresses our procurement concerns. We will:

- Give dataset access on 7/5 (done).
- Proceed with the POC kickoff on 7/6.
- Ask legal to push a 60-day review window; procurement is fine with the 10% interim credit transformable to invoice credit if SLOs are missed.

Procurement has attached a short PO template (Acme_PO_Draft.docx) for Redwood to review. Please route the SLA appendix via DocuSign (the link you shared) and I'll have our ML infra lead join the 7/6 kickoff.

Jordan Smith

Acme Health
